facts.reason: Misleading by omission. The MSBOC FAQ (official) says subcontractors performing residential electrical, mechanical, HVAC or plumbing work must be licensed by MSBOC, with no dollar threshold, while the $50,000 threshold applies to commercial jobs. The no-statewide-individual-trade-license point is still not confirmed, so status stays unverified.

fixed.fact: Mississippi does not license journeyman or master electricians, plumbers or HVAC technicians statewide; individual trade licenses, where required, come from cities and counties. The Mississippi State Board of Contractors licenses companies: a commercial license is needed for contractors and subcontractors on commercial jobs over $50,000, and electrical, mechanical/HVAC and plumbing subcontractors on residential projects must hold an MSBOC license at any contract amount.

facts.reason: Ala. Admin. Code r. 440-X-3-.04 says an applicant who fails the first time may, on request, take an equivalent practical exam, and that practical exam must be taken within six months of the failed attempt; the fact implied a general retake-or-practical option both within six months.

fixed.fact: Alabama HVACR certification can be earned by exam or by reciprocity (for licensees from reciprocal states with no past or pending discipline). existing.reason: License names were off. The CT DCP 'Plumbing Licenses and Scope of Work' page calls P-1 the 'Unlimited Plumbing Contractor' (not 'Plumbing and Piping Contractor') and P-2 the 'Unlimited Journeyperson Plumber'; P-1 needs 2 years as an unlimited licensed journeyperson (or equivalent), P-2 needs a registered apprenticeship (or equivalent) and works only while employed by a licensed contractor. Board name (Plumbing and Piping Work Examining Board) appears in DCP's own document paths. Matches new fact S5A-36.

fixed.fact: Connecticut plumbers are licensed by the Department of Consumer Protection (Plumbing and Piping Work Examining Board). The P-1 Unlimited Plumbing Contractor needs 2 years as an unlimited licensed journeyperson (or equivalent experience and training), and the P-2 Unlimited Journeyperson Plumber needs a registered apprenticeship (or equivalent) and may work only while employed by a licensed contractor. Limited categories include J-1/J-2 (domestic water pumps and water conditioning) and P-6/P-7 (sewer, storm and water lines).

existing.reason: Conflicts with the DLCP Electrician license guide (and new fact S5A-45): a DC master electrician by exam needs 8 years (16,000 work hours) of experience, not 'several years as a licensed journeyman'; a journeyman needs 4 years (8,000 hours); an approved apprenticeship can waive the journeyman exam; exams are open book.

fixed.fact: DC electricians are licensed as apprentice, journeyman and master. A journeyman by exam needs 4 years (8,000 work hours) and a master needs 8 years (16,000 work hours) of experience; a completed nationally certified apprenticeship can waive the journeyman exam, and the exams are open book. An electrical contractor must designate a DC-licensed master electrician.
